title: 📘 UNIT 2: MAJOR SPOTS OF ANCIENT WORLD CIVILIZATIONS UP TO c.500 A.D
notes:
Ancient civilizations developed mainly after the Neolithic/Agricultural Revolution.

Common features → organized government, specialized work, social classes, complex religion, trade, arts and architecture.

Major regions → Africa + Asia + Europe + Latin America.

title: 2.1 🌍 Ancient Civilizations of Africa
notes:
Major African civilizations studied → Ancient Egypt and Kush-Meroe.

River valleys, agriculture, trade and natural resources supported the development of these civilizations.

title: 2.1.1 🇪🇬 Ancient Egypt
notes:
Egypt developed along the Nile River, called the 'Gift of the Nile' by Herodotus.

Upper Egypt → south.
Lower Egypt → north and Nile Delta.

c.3100 B.C → Menes united Upper and Lower Egypt and established Memphis as the capital.

Main periods → Old Kingdom + Middle Kingdom + New Kingdom.

Pharaoh → absolute ruler considered both human and divine.

title: 2.1.1.1 🏺 Egyptian Civilization and Achievements
notes:
Major achievements:
• Hieroglyphic writing.
• Papyrus.
• Mathematics and geometry.
• Calendar and astronomy.
• Medicine and surgery.
• Irrigation agriculture.
• Pyramids and monumental architecture.
• Mummification.
• Trade and organized government.

Religion → mainly polytheistic with strong belief in the afterlife.

title: 2.1.2 🐪 Kush-Meroe
notes:
Kush → ancient civilization in Nubia along the Nile south of Egypt.

📍 Main capitals → Napata → Meroe.

Piankhi → conquered Egypt and established the 25th Egyptian Dynasty.

c.590 B.C → Meroe replaced Napata as capital.

Meroe prospered through trade and access to gold and iron.

title: 2.1.2.1 🔥 Achievements and Decline of Meroe
notes:
Major achievements:
• Iron smelting.
• Own language and writing system.
• Distinct art and architecture.
• Long-distance trade.
• Gold and iron production.

Major exports → ivory, slaves, skins, ostrich feathers, ebony and gold.

Decline → rivalry with Aksum.

4th century A.D → Aksumite king Ezana invaded and destroyed Meroe, ending the Kushite kingdom.

title: 2.2 🌏 Civilizations in Asia
notes:
Major Asian civilizations → Mesopotamia + India + China.

Most early civilizations developed around major river systems and became centers of agriculture, trade, government and technology.

title: 2.2.1 🏺 Mesopotamia
notes:
Mesopotamia → 'land between rivers' → Tigris and Euphrates.

Sumerian civilization → developed around 2900 B.C.

Sumerian political units → independent city-states ruled by kings called Lugals.

Major civilizations → Sumerians + Babylonians + Assyrians + Persians.

title: 2.2.1.1 ✍️ Sumerians
notes:
Major achievements:
• Cuneiform writing.
• Plough.
• Irrigation.
• City-state government.
• Mathematics and astronomy.
• Wheel and other technologies.

📌 Cuneiform → one of the earliest known writing systems.

title: 2.2.1.2 ⚖️ Babylon and Hammurabi
notes:
Babylon → major Mesopotamian kingdom.

Hammurabi → famous Babylonian king.

Code of Hammurabi → written collection of laws regulating social, economic and legal life.

Principle → punishments depended on the social status and nature of the offense.

📌 Important contribution → development of written law and organized administration.

title: 2.2.1.3 ⚔️ Assyria
notes:
Assyrians → powerful military state in northern Mesopotamia.

Major contributions:
• Advanced military organization.
• Iron weapons.
• Siege warfare.
• Efficient administration.
• Large territorial empire.

📌 Military strength was a major basis of Assyrian expansion.

title: 2.2.1.4 🏹 Persian Empire
notes:
Persian Empire → founded by Cyrus the Great.

Government → divided into provinces called satrapies, ruled by satraps.

Darius I → organized administration and issued gold currency called darics.

Major developments → irrigation, trade, roads and efficient administration.

Zoroastrianism → founded by Zoroaster/Zarathustra; emphasized the struggle between good and evil.

331 B.C → Alexander the Great conquered the Persian Empire.

title: 2.2.2 🇮🇳 Ancient India
notes:
Indus Valley Civilization → developed around 2500 B.C along the Indus River.

Major cities → Harappa + Mohenjo-daro.

Features → planned streets, brick buildings, water supply and drainage systems.

Early population → Dravidians.

Later → Indo-Aryans moved into northern India and established new states.

title: 2.2.2.1 🕉️ Hinduism and Buddhism
notes:
Hinduism → developed from early Indo-Aryan beliefs.

Key idea → cycle of rebirths; salvation through spiritual development and other paths.

Buddhism → founded by Siddhartha Gautama (c.563–483 B.C.).

Middle Way → avoids extreme asceticism and extreme materialism.

Buddhism spread → Southeast Asia + China + Japan.

title: 2.2.2.2 🔢 Indian Achievements
notes:
Major achievements:
• Mathematics.
• Decimal system.
• Zero.
• Numerals later known as Arabic numerals.
• Surgery and medicine.
• Use of medicinal herbs.
• Chemistry and metalworking.
• Production of steel, glass, soap and cement.

title: 2.2.3 🇨🇳 Ancient China
notes:
Early Chinese civilization → Huang-He/Yellow River region.

First dynasty → Shang Dynasty (c.1700–1122 B.C.).

Shang achievements → bronze vessels, horse-drawn war chariots and writing.

Zhou Dynasty → followed Shang and ruled until 256 B.C.

Warring States Period → 403–221 B.C.

221 B.C → Qin defeated rivals and established China's first empire.

title: 2.2.3.1 🧠 Confucianism and Legalism
notes:
Confucius (551–479 B.C.) → emphasized moral character, responsibility and proper social relationships.

Five relationships → ruler–subject + father–son + husband–wife + elder brother–younger brother + friend–friend.

Legalism → emphasized authority, strict laws and efficient administration.

Qin Shi Huang → used Legalist principles to centralize and unify China.

title: 2.2.3.2 🧪 Chinese Achievements
notes:
Major achievements:
• Silk production and trade.
• Paper.
• Printing.
• Gunpowder.
• Porcelain.
• Wheelbarrow.
• Varnish.
• Use of coal.
• Chinese writing system.

📌 Silk → important Chinese industry and major trade commodity.

title: 2.3 🏛️ Civilizations in Europe
notes:
Major European civilizations → Ancient Greece + Ancient Rome.

Greek civilization → city-states, philosophy, democracy, arts and sciences.

Roman civilization → republic, empire, law, engineering and administration.

title: 2.3.1 🇬🇷 Ancient Greece
notes:
Greek civilization → developed around independent city-states called polis.

Major city-states → Athens + Sparta.

Athens → democracy, philosophy, arts and learning.
Sparta → strong military society.

Greek civilization strongly influenced philosophy, politics, science, medicine, history and art.

title: 2.3.1.1 🗳️ Athenian Democracy
notes:
Athens developed direct democracy.

Citizens → adult male citizens could participate directly in government.

Assembly → citizens debated and voted on laws and government policies.

⚠️ Women and slaves were excluded from political participation.

Direct democracy → citizens participate directly in decision-making.
Representative democracy → citizens elect representatives to make decisions.

title: 2.3.1.2 🧠 Greek Contributions and Hellenistic Age
notes:
Philosophers → Socrates + Plato + Aristotle.

History → Herodotus + Thucydides.
Medicine → Hippocrates.

Other achievements → mathematics, physics, biology, architecture, sculpture, drama and philosophy.

431–404 B.C → Peloponnesian War; Athens was defeated by Sparta.

Alexander the Great → spread Greek language and culture into Egypt and Asia.

Hellenistic Age → Greek culture blended with cultures of Asia and Africa after Alexander's conquests.

title: 2.3.2 🦅 Ancient Rome
notes:
Traditional founding → 753 B.C by Romulus and Remus.

509 B.C → Roman Republic established after overthrow of monarchy.

Senate → powerful institution of the Republic.

Social classes → Patricians + Equites + Plebeians.

Manumission → freeing of slaves.

title: 2.3.2.1 ⚔️ Roman Expansion and Empire
notes:
Roman expansion → conquered Italy and later territories around the Mediterranean.

Punic Wars → Rome fought Carthage for control of the Mediterranean.

Julius Caesar → became sole ruler; assassinated in 44 B.C.

Octavian/Augustus → became first Roman emperor in 27 B.C.

Pax Romana → about 200 years of Roman peace, stability and prosperity.

title: 2.3.2.2 🏗️ Roman Achievements and Decline
notes:
Major achievements:
• Roman law.
• Roads and bridges.
• Aqueducts.
• Military organization.
• Government and administration.
• Latin language.
• Architecture → Colosseum, Forum and temples.

395 A.D → Roman Empire divided into West and East.
476 A.D → Western Roman Empire collapsed.
1453 → Byzantine Empire finally fell to the Ottoman Turks.

title: 2.4 🌎 Civilizations in Latin America
notes:
Major civilizations → Maya + Aztecs + Incas.

Agriculture and domestication of plants and animals supported permanent settlements and population growth.

Major crops → maize, beans, squash, cassava and sweet potatoes.

title: 2.4.1 🗿 The Maya
notes:
Maya → developed large cities in Mesoamerica.

Classic Period → began around 250 A.D.

Political system → independent city-states; important centers included Tikal and Calakmul.

Economy → mainly agriculture and trade.

Major crops → maize, beans and squash.

Achievements → hieroglyphic writing + mathematics + astronomy + 365-day calendar + concept of zero + monumental temples and pyramids.

title: 2.4.2 🦅 The Aztecs
notes:
1200s A.D → Aztecs moved into the Valley of Mexico.

1325 → established Tenochtitlan.

Government → powerful emperor with officials controlling justice and trade.

Economy → agriculture, tribute and trade.

Achievements → roads + floating gardens + astronomy + mathematics + 365-day calendar + medicine.

Religion → polytheistic; included human sacrifice.

title: 2.4.3 ☀️ The Incas
notes:
c.1450 → Inca founded the last great empire in the Andes.

Territory → present-day Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, Chile and Argentina.

Government → absolute emperor + provinces governed by nobles.

Capital → Cuzco.

Religion → emperor regarded as son of Inti, the sun god.

Achievements → roads + terraces + advanced stone construction + irrigation + measurement + brain surgery + use of quinine.

title: 2.5 ✝️ The Rise and Spread of Christianity
notes:
Christianity arose among the followers of Jesus in Roman-controlled Judea.

Jesus → emphasized love of God, love of neighbor and forgiveness.

c.30 A.D → Jesus was crucified.

Early Christians → first mainly Jews, later many Gentiles joined Christianity.

Christian communities → led by bishops; later archbishops and patriarchs developed.

title: 2.5.1 ⛪ Early Christian Organization and Heresies
notes:
Five major patriarchates → Rome + Alexandria + Antioch + Constantinople + Jerusalem.

Pope → bishop/patriarch of Rome.

Monasticism → developed from about the 3rd century; monks lived in communities or as hermits.

Heresy → doctrine rejected and condemned by the Church.

Church councils → meetings of church leaders to establish and clarify doctrine.

title: 2.5.2 📜 Councils of Nicaea and Constantinople
notes:
Council of Nicaea → 325 A.D.

📌 Addressed major disputes concerning Christian doctrine and rejected Arianism.

Council of Constantinople → 381 A.D.

📌 Confirmed and developed the Nicene formulation of Christian belief, including teaching concerning the Holy Spirit.

title: 2.5.3 🕊️ Christianity in the Roman Empire
notes:
Early Christians experienced periods of Roman persecution.

313 A.D → Edict of Milan granted religious toleration to Christians.

Constantine → supported Christianity.

Christianity later became the official religion of the Roman Empire.

📌 Christianity transformed religious, moral and cultural life in the ancient world.

title: 2.5.4 🇪🇹 Christianity and Ethiopia
notes:
Christianity entered Aksum during the 4th century A.D.

Frumentius → converted King Ezana and became the first bishop of Ethiopia.

Ezana's later coins → carried the Christian cross.

Nine Saints → helped spread Christianity and monasticism.

Major contributions → Ge'ez Bible translation + liturgy + literature + church architecture.

Saint Yared → associated with Ethiopian church liturgy and hymns.

title: 🏆 UNIT 2 — MUST REMEMBER
notes:
🌍 Ancient civilizations → developed strongly after the Agricultural/Neolithic Revolution.

🇪🇬 Egypt → Nile + Pharaoh + hieroglyphics + pyramids + afterlife.
🐪 Kush-Meroe → Napata → Meroe + ironworking + trade → decline after Aksumite attack.

🏺 Mesopotamia → Tigris + Euphrates + Sumer + cuneiform + Hammurabi + Assyria + Persia.
🇮🇳 India → Indus Valley + Harappa + Mohenjo-daro + Hinduism + Buddhism + zero + decimal system.
🇨🇳 China → Shang + Zhou + Qin + Confucianism + Legalism + paper + printing + gunpowder + silk.

🇬🇷 Greece → polis + Athens + democracy + philosophy + Alexander + Hellenistic Age.
🦅 Rome → Republic + Senate + Punic Wars + Caesar + Augustus + Pax Romana + Roman law.

🌎 Maya → city-states + calendar + zero + writing.
🦅 Aztecs → Tenochtitlan + tribute + floating gardens + medicine.
☀️ Incas → Cuzco + roads + terraces + stonework + quinine.

✝️ Christianity → Jesus → early Church → Nicaea (325) → Constantinople (381) → spread through Roman world.
🇪🇹 Ethiopia → Frumentius → King Ezana → Nine Saints → Ge'ez Christianity.
